Fulness of Time
FOOL-ness uv tym
noun phrase (Galatians 4:4)
From the Authorized Version rendering of the Greek to pleroma tou chronou, “the fulness of the time”; the appointed and ripened moment of Christ's coming.

📖 Biblical Definition

The fulness of time is the appointed and ripened moment, ordained from eternity, at which God sent forth His Son into the world. “When the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, to redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.” The phrase declares that the incarnation came neither too soon nor too late but at the exact hour set by the providence of God, when all things were ready. The dictionary marks the manifold ways in which the time was full: the types and prophecies of the old covenant had run their course and ripened toward their substance; the Roman peace and roads opened the world to the spread of the gospel; the Greek tongue gave a common speech for the apostles; the Jewish dispersion and synagogue prepared a hearing among the nations; and the long failure of the law to make men righteous had exposed the need of a Saviour. So the four hundred silent years and all the centuries before were not empty waiting but God ordering the stage. Mark records the Lord's own announcement at His coming: “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.” The dictionary holds the fulness of time as a witness to the meticulous providence of God over history: He governs the rise and fall of empires, the spread of languages, the ripening of expectation, all to the end that His Son should come at the perfect hour to redeem His people.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The appointed, ripened moment ordained by God at which He sent forth His Son (Galatians 4:4); a witness to the meticulous providence that ordered history so Christ should come at the perfect hour.

FULNESS OF TIME, noun phrase. [Greek to pleroma tou chronou.] The appointed, ripened moment of Christ's coming.

“When the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son” (Galatians 4:4).

The types and prophecies had ripened; the world was prepared by language, roads, and dispersion.

It witnesses to God's meticulous providence over the course of history.

The Lord announced it: “The time is fulfilled… repent ye, and believe the gospel” (Mark 1:15).

📖 Key Scripture

Ga 4:4 — "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,"

Ga 4:5 — "To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons."

Eph 1:10 — "That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him:"

Mr 1:15 — "And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition; the danger is a deistic or merely sociological reading that credits the timing of Christ's coming to historical accident rather than the providence of God.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is meticulous providence. A common modern habit explains the timing of Christianity's rise by purely sociological causes—Roman roads, Greek language, political stability—as though these were happy accidents that a clever movement exploited. The dictionary affirms the historical means but denies the deism. Paul says God sent forth His Son when the fulness of the time was come; the means were themselves ordered by the God who governs the rise and fall of empires to the precise end of redemption.

The phrase also rebukes the impatience of the human heart, which questions why God delayed so long or acts so slowly still. The fulness of time teaches that God's appointments are never early and never late; the centuries of promise, the silent years, the long exposure of the law's inability to justify—all ripened the hour. The same providence that timed the first advent governs the second, so the believer waits in patience, knowing the kingdom comes, and shall be consummated, at the hour the Father has set.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Greek pleroma (fulness, that which fills) and chronos (time); the time was “full” as a vessel filled to the appointed measure.

expand to see more

Pleroma, Greek, fulness, completion, that which fills up.

Chronos, Greek, time as duration, the appointed span now run out.

Kairos, Greek, the fitting or opportune moment, kin to the idea of ripeness.

The “dispensation of the fulness of times” (Ephesians 1:10) sets it in God's ordering of all ages.

“The time is fulfilled” (Mark 1:15, peplerotai ho kairos) is the Lord's own announcement.

Usage

"The teacher showed that God ordered roads, tongues, and empires to bring His Son in the fulness of time."

"He comforted the impatient with the truth that God's appointments are never early and never late."

"She saw the four hundred silent years not as empty waiting but as the ripening of the appointed hour."
